_comment: Per-model label canonicalisation for the discogs-effnet 400-class style model. Discogs uses `Parent---Substyle` format with `---` as separator (e.g. 'Electronic---Tech House'). The .NET normaliser turns `---` into spaces and the resolver finds parent+substyle naturally — 211 of 400 labels match without any remap entry. Coverage map below was generated by /tmp/raytagger-remap-analysis/analyzer.py against the full 400-class vocabulary; see docs/PLAN_GENRE_CLASSIFICATION.md §4.0a.
_section_drum_and_bass_alias: Discogs writes 'Drum n Bass' — the 'n' lacks the surrounding boundaries to be 'and'. Without this remap the resolver finds neither the genre nor any subgenre.
_section_subgenre_only_labels: These labels are subgenres in our taxonomy but the model emits them under the 'Electronic' parent. Resolver needs a parent before searching subgenres, so we explicitly route them.
_section_funk_soul_tiebreak: Parent 'Funk / Soul' lowercases+normalises to 'funk soul ...'. Resolver finds Funk, Soul, AND R&B as whole-word hits; same length, tiebreak by YAML order puts Funk first — but the substyle clearly says R&B. Remap forces the correct parent.
_section_skipped_ambiguous: Labels deliberately NOT remapped — single-word substyles under Electronic that could map to multiple taxonomy entries (Acid → Techno/House/Trance? Dub → Techno subgenre vs Reggae? Disco → 70s vs Disco House? Industrial → Techno subgenre vs industrial rock? Minimal → House/Techno/DnB?). Latin---* (29 styles), Reggae---* (3 styles), Blues---*, Classical---*, Folk/World/Country---*, Brass & Military---*, Stage & Screen---*, Non-Music---*, Children's---* are all out-of-vocabulary for the current taxonomy and correctly drop. The `Hip Hop---*` and `Electronic---Lo-fi` parent labels resolve naturally via the normaliser (no remap needed; hyphenated taxonomy entries like 'Lo-fi' remain a known limitation tracked in §4.0a).
